correctness.rationale: All essential inferences and computations verified by independent replay. Verifier re-run in fresh process passes: 186 Latin squares, 5 transversal witnesses and 1 partial witness all satisfy row/col/symbol distinctness and match matrices, with independent permutation recounts N=133 (Z7), N=0 (Z8), N=384 (C4xC2, C2^3, D8, Q8) exactly as claimed. Auditor independently recounted N for all 6 bases via itertools.permutations (133/0/384/384/384/384) and validated all transversal/partial cell lists against matrices. Group axioms and element-order invariants confirmed (Z7 [1,7x6]; Z8 [1,2,4,4,8x4]; C4xC2 [1,2x3,4x4]; C2^3 [1,2x7]; D8 [1,2x5,4x2] non-abelian center 2; Q8 [1,2,4x6] non-abelian center 2), confirming five order-8 bases are pairwise non-isomorphic groups. Isotopy logic sound: tau/N invariance under row/col/symbol permutations is elementary and correctly proved; seeded isotopes are isotopic by construction so per-stratum constancy is theorem, additionally spot-checked computationally. Independent backtracking isotopy implementation reproduced claimed node counts exactly (C2^3 vs D8 non-isotopic with 521 nodes; Z7_base vs Z7_iso00 isotopic with 17 nodes), corroborating exhaustive-search logs and 15 rep-pair distinctness certificates plus n-mismatch handling. Tau maximality correctly derived: for N>0 reps tau=n follows from exhibited transversal; for Z8 N=0 exhaustive unsatisfiability (3705-node DFS + perm recount 0) plus exhibited size-7 partial certifies tau=7=n-1. Hall-Paige consistency holds (cyclic Sylow Z8 transversal-free; others non-cyclic/trivial Sylow transversal-rich). Proof vs computation properly separated in DRAFT; no boundary error, no conflation of experimental evidence with theorem. No correctness defect found.

originality.rationale: Narrow computational novelty granted after live retrieval. Nearest priors found: Montgomery 2024 decade survey (existence/asymptotics/structure, no seeded isotopy tau/N census with witnesses for orders 7-8); Wanless 2009 survey with dedicated group-table/orthomorphism/covering-radii section (conjectures and Hall-Paige background, no exact N=133/384 table for these six tables); Cavenagh-Wanless 2017 (explicitly states even-order cyclic addition table B_n has no transversals, directly anticipating the Z8 N=0 row, plus asymptotic species lower bound and k-plex constructions, not a stratum-maximum table); Hall-Paige 1955 necessity plus Wilcox-Evans-Bray sufficiency (complete mappings equivalent to group-table transversals; Sylow-2 trivial-or-noncyclic condition predicts exactly the observed existence pattern Z7 yes / Z8 no / other four yes, so qualitative pattern is textbook). No retrieved source tabulates the exact tau/N values 7/133, 7/0, 8/384 for these six normalized tables together with per-representative exact counts and CSV replay witnesses, nor the specific 30-seed (5757+k) isotopy-neighbourhood package. A failed search does not prove global priority, but on inspected evidence the exact witness package is absent from surveys and Hall-Paige literature, which are existence/asymptotic/constructional. Hence the precise N-count table is treated as narrowly new. Qualitative content (which groups have transversals; isotopy invariance; Albert isotopic-groups-are-isomorphic observation) is prior art and is discounted toward value, not counted as novelty.

value.rationale: Even taking correctness and narrow novelty as given, the result is not independently worth finding later. It combines four reject categories the brief explicitly warns against. (1) Textbook restatement: the scientifically meaningful pattern (Z8 transversal-free; all other listed groups transversal-rich) is a direct corollary of Hall-Paige (1955 conjecture, proved 2009 via CFSG), acknowledged in DRAFT sec 4.3 as sanity check; isotopy invariance of tau/N is elementary one-paragraph proof; collapse via Albert's theorem is textbook. (2) Mere parameter substitution: strata are 30 seeded row/col/symbol permutations with arbitrary seed 5757+k plus base (186 squares); by construction every isotope is isotopic to its base, so 186->6 collapse is tautological (DRAFT sec 2.2/6 admits no isotope can beat baseline, theoretically impossible). The seed count, seed value, and choice of orders 7-8 add no conceptual stratification. (3) Tiny unmotivated gain / unexplained enumeration: the only potentially new numbers are N=133 and N=384 (x4), obtained in seconds by brute force for n<=8 (40320 perms max, ~3k DFS nodes), with no structural explanation — DRAFT sec 6.3 admits N=384 coincidence across four non-isomorphic groups is verified computation, not theorem, left open. No new infinite family (disclaimed), no surprising distribution (no beating isotope, impossible), no downstream use. (4) Scope disclaimer empties significance: DRAFT sec 6.1 stresses this is not a full order-7/8 census (which numbers in millions/billions per main class) but six group tables only. A seconds-scale table of six small-group transversal counts with redundant isotopic copies and no theory is a routine exercise, not a citable micro-census others would independently seek. Correct and narrowly new yet not valuable => REJECT per value-failure rule.

Live literature comparison: inspected surveys and Hall-Paige lineage confirm qualitative pattern is prior (Cavenagh-Wanless well-known even-B_n transversal-free; Hall-Paige Sylow condition); no source found tabulating exact 133/384 seeded-stratum table, supporting narrow originality but value failure as arbitrary small-n brute force without theory.

sources.title: Transversals in Latin Squares — Richard Montgomery (2024 survey)

sources.comparison: 22-page survey covering existence/enumeration, plexes, dedicated group-table/complete-mapping/orthomorphism section and covering radii with open problems; discusses Hall-Paige and orthomorphisms but publishes no exhaustive tau/N=133/384 table for seeded isotopes of all groups of orders 7-8.
sources.title: Transversals in Latin Squares — Ian M. Wanless (2009 survey)

sources.comparison: Proves lower bound n^{n^{3/2}(1/2-o(1))} on transversal-free species and k-plex constructions settling 2002 conjecture; abstract explicitly states it is well known that even-order cyclic addition table B_n has no transversals, directly anticipating the Z8 N=0 row, but provides no seeded tau/N maximum table.
sources.title: Latin squares with no transversals — Cavenagh and Wanless

sources.comparison: States complete mappings of G are equivalent to transversals of the Cayley table and Hall-Paige Sylow-2 trivial-or-noncyclic condition; this theorem predicts exactly the observed pattern (Z7/C4xC2/C2^3/D8/Q8 have transversals, Z8 does not), so qualitative existence is prior art, not new.
sources.title: Reduction of the Hall-Paige conjecture to sporadic simple groups — Stewart Wilcox

sources.comparison: Original 1955 Pacific J. Math. paper proving Sylow-2 necessity for complete mappings (transversals of group tables); provides the textbook criterion that already decides the existence side for all six tables in this census, leaving only seconds-scale exact N counts as potentially new.
sources.title: Complete mappings of finite groups — Hall and Paige

residual_risks: Full 186-square permutation recount not re-run exhaustively by auditor (reps + theorem + selfcheck.log 0-mismatch claim relied upon); risk negligible given isotopy-invariance theorem plus spot checks, but not every seeded matrix independently recounted.

All 645 isotopy_log rows not individually re-verified; only representative pairs re-searched with independent code (exact node-count reproduction for two cases mitigates fabrication risk but does not exhaustively certify every log line).

Literature search was live but bounded (arXiv + Crossref queries, 5 sources inspected); global priority cannot be proved — an obscure table containing N=133/384 could exist outside retrieved set; originality PASS is therefore narrow and evidence-relative.

N counting convention (rows ordered, one per column perm) matches standard transversal count and verifier, but alternative normalizations (e.g., normalized/transversal equivalence classes) would give different numbers; reuse must preserve convention.
